newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Jan-Apr trade deficit falls 9.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Jan-Apr trade deficit falls 9.3 percent.

text.p: Peru's trade deficit fell 9.3 percent in the first four months of 1997 to $496 million from $547 million in the same period last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Friday.

Exports grew 12.2 percent in the first four months to $2.088 billion, compared with the same period the year before, the bank added in its weekly report. Imports were $2.584 billion in the first four months, up 7.4 percent compared with the same period in 1996.
Traditional exports grew 4.3 percent to $1.435 billion, while non-traditional exports rose 38.2 percent to $631 million, and the bank's category of "other" exports fell 19.7 percent to $22 million.

Among imports, consumer goods fell 4.1 percent to $546 million, and raw materials fell 1.0 percent to $1.031 billion, while capital goods gained 26.8 percent to $930 million and "other" goods were up 22.6 percent to $77 million.
Peru's trade deficit fell 9.0 percent in 1996 to $1.996 billion from $2.185 billion in 1995, according to the bank.
